learning_objective: The learner will classify each of eight situations by the media alternative it calls for (captions, transcript, or audio description), with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** media-alternative-matcher
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Understand
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will classify each of eight situations by the media alternative it calls for (captions, transcript, or audio description), with at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** Captions, Transcript, Audio Description (all defined in this chapter above this block). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each situation the learner commits one of three alternatives. A choice is correct when it matches the Correct alternative column in Content. Mastery is at least 7 of 8 correct on the first attempt. Reading the definitions is exploration, not evidence. **Misconceptions:** (1) A transcript replaces captions. (2) Audio description is only for blind learners watching films. (3) Captions help only deaf learners. **Instructional Rationale:** Classifying a need by its alternative is an Understand-level action. Eight situations that vary the learner and the barrier teach the learner to ask what is missing: the sound, the sight, or a readable text. **Content:** The three alternatives: Captions (timed text of speech and sounds), Transcript (a separate text document of the audio and the key visual information), Audio description (narration of important visual information). The eight situations: | # | Situation shown to the learner | Correct alternative | Why (shown as feedback) | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | A deaf learner watches a lecture video. | Captions | The learner needs the speech as timed text. | | 2 | A blind learner watches a science demonstration in which the steps appear only on screen. | Audio description | The visual steps are not in the audio. | | 3 | A learner wants to search a podcast for a quotation. | Transcript | Text can be searched, and audio alone cannot. | | 4 | A learner watches a video in a noisy cafeteria with the sound off. | Captions | Timed text lets the learner follow without sound. | | 5 | A learner who is deaf and blind reads a video's content on a braille display. | Transcript | A text document can be read in braille. | | 6 | A video shows a chart that the narrator never describes. | Audio description | The chart is visual information that the audio leaves out. | | 7 | A learner with a reading difference prefers to read at their own pace instead of watching. | Transcript | A document lets the learner set the pace. | | 8 | A learner still learning the language wants to follow the words on screen as they are spoken. | Captions | Timed text matches the speech as it is said. | **Provenance:** The situations are illustrative cases written for this chapter, and the sim labels them "illustrative examples". The definitions follow the chapter sections "Captions", "Transcript", and "Audio Description". **Rules:** Each situation has exactly one correct alternative. Three situations call for Captions, three for Transcript, and two for Audio description. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner sees one situation and the three alternatives. 2. The learner chooses an alternative, and the choice is committed. 3. The sim shows whether it was correct and the Why text. 4. After situation 8 the sim shows the summary. **Feedback:** 8 situations in a shuffled order, one attempt each. Correct: "Correct: [alternative]. [Why]". Incorrect: "Not quite. This calls for [alternative]. [Why]". The summary shows "[n] of 8 correct on the first attempt". At 7 or more it adds "You can match the need to the alternative." Below 7 it lists the Why text of each missed situation. **Starting State:** The first situation and the three alternatives. The question shown is "What does this learner need?" **Chapter Anchors:** The chapter says captions are timed text, a transcript is a separate text document, and audio description narrates visual information the audio omits.
